digests.summary: The spine is a 3,058-row catalogue (snapshot_v1.jsonl, taken 16 Oct 00:50Z, validators fork 688174f plus upstream 74da0ec, renders X_ITE 16.5.0), not a pile of files on disk. Only 974 scene bodies sit in /mnt/project-files (585 of them licence-clean); the other 2,084 live in a GCS tuning tarball (1,610) or the X3DJSONLD mirror at d2525fe (474), and captions, 11,796 embedding vectors and 2,364 scenes' renders are BigQuery/GCS-only (no GCP access used here). Licence-clean is 2,205, but 2,153 of those are our own model outputs (1,610 tuned-eval) and only 52 carry an explicit permissive licence. Clean-and-valid-on-both is 576, which collapse to 236 distinct node-sets. Hands-on on bpy 5.2.3 with x3d-blender-io main 482741b, over the 585 clean on-disk scenes: 568 import, all 16 exceptions are on fork-invalid inputs, and 568/568 X3D 4.0 re-exports validate on fork d5598c4 and upstream 74da0ec, including 211 inputs the fork rejected. That means the exporter launders invalidity, so the Blender-lane benchmark must score fidelity, not validity. The spine's mutation operators regenerate deterministically: on 74 clean valid bases they gave 3,649 mutants, 374 of which crash the importer, and 293 of those pass fork d5598c4 and upstream 74da0ec but are all caught by the PR #8 branch (399e6c5). The corpus is a breadth and robustness set (primitives, PBR, animation, HAnim), not science-viz: it has zero clean valid PointSet, ColorRGBA, MetadataFloat or volume scenes, and only 5 clean splat scenes (SH0 only). Splat round trips are exact on 5/5, but the 140k-splat one fails XSD at every validator commit tested on the libxml2 10 MB limit alone.

offers_to_blender: A licence-clean importer test corpus: 585 on-disk scenes (356 valid on fork d5598c4 and upstream 74da0ec) and a 111-scene Tier A list (one smallest representative per distinct node-set, clean, valid on both, round-trip stable on faces/bbox/objects/materials, 4.2 MB total).

An expected-loss table measured on 568 imports: Box/Sphere/Cylinder/Cone bake to IndexedFaceSet, Material becomes PhysicalMaterial, Normal and WorldInfo are dropped, ROUTE survives in only 54.5% of scenes.
A deterministic robustness mutant generator (51 operators + 9 controls) and a crash-site list in import_x3d.py: lines 1651, 2152, 2208, 2234, 2316, 2563, 2607, 4300.
A ranked list of unhandled nodes by corpus frequency to steer importer work: GeoLocation, GeoViewpoint, Script, TouchSensor, ColorInterpolator, ProtoInstance.
Exemplar retrieval offline (node bag, Qwen3 embeddings, 12 archetype clusters) and an E1 harness to host a Blender arm.
Validator hint text that names the fix (profile-component-fix) and the autofix result, reusable as agent feedback after a bpy export.
Five licence-clean splat scenes (2 to 140,000 splats) plus a measured exact PLY-free X3D 4.1 round trip on bpy 5.2.3.
offers_to_x3d: Real-importer evidence that validator gaps are not academic: all 293 count/index mutants that crash the importer pass fork d5598c4 and upstream 74da0ec, and PR #8's checks (399e6c5) flag 293/293 with 0 false alarms on 354 controls.

A reproducible case that validate_xml lacks huge_tree: an 11.3 MB single-node splat export fails XSD at 688174f, d5598c4, 74da0ec and fork main 8dd0d3e, while the semantic pass already uses huge_tree (semantic.py _PARSER).
568 Blender-produced X3D 4.0 files (from 568 distinct clean inputs) that all validate, usable as a third-party-writer corpus for the validator.
A branch-topology warning: fork main 8dd0d3e does not contain PR #7 (d5598c4) or PR #8 (399e6c5); both live only on integration/validator-fixes (acdf5c4).
A classifier fix list for the spine's licence regexes: GPL, LGPL and Unlicense read as unknown, 'NONE' reads as unknown, CC BY-ND reads as permissive.

Natural-defect and mutant fixtures with the validator verdict attached, so upstream-vs-fork differences (399 false alarms on MetadataString controls at 74da0ec; two clean splat scenes rejected for GaussianSplats.metadata=MetadataSet) are demonstrable on real files.

bridge_ideas.idea: Importer-must-not-raise suite built from spine mutants: a small bpy test running ~8 deterministic operators (wrong_arity, texcoordindex_oob, colorindex_oob, normalindex_oob, elevation_count, coordindex_oob, plus Extrusion/LineSet cases) on 3 tiny clean bases, expecting FINISHED plus a logged warning, never an exception. Public-repo friendly; no AI trailers on x3d_mcp commits.
bridge_ideas.evidence: 374 of 3,012 defect mutants (12.4%) raised in x3d-blender-io 482741b on bpy 5.2.3: translation arity ValueError at import_x3d.py:1651 (39), Vector() at 4300 (11), None '<' float (21), IndexError at 2234/2208/2152 (texCoordIndex/colorIndex/normalIndex 73-74 each, coordIndex 10) and 2316 (ElevationGrid height 73); plus 2 natural bugs (Extrusion ZeroDivisionError at 2563, LineSet without Coordinate at 2607) and 13 malformed-XML SAXParseExceptions. Files: scratch bpy/sweep_*.jsonl.

bridge_ideas.idea: Use the validator as the pre-import gate in the Blender lane, pinned to integration/validator-fixes at or after 399e6c5 (not fork main 8dd0d3e, not d5598c4). Report the finding text to the agent as the repair signal.
bridge_ideas.evidence: v2 mutants on 74 clean valid bases: 293/293 importer IndexErrors pass fork d5598c4 and upstream 74da0ec (0 flagged) but 399e6c5 flags 293/293 with 0 flags on 354 controls (val/mut2_399e6c5.jsonl). v1: d5598c4 flags 81/81 crash mutants, upstream 71/81. git merge-base: 399e6c5 and d5598c4 are ancestors of origin/integration/validator-fixes, not of origin/main 8dd0d3e.

bridge_ideas.idea: Score the agents-in-Blender vs x3d_mcp comparison on fidelity, not validity. The exporter launders invalidity, so a validity metric would hand the Blender lane a free 100%. Use the Y8 render-completeness judge, a parts/placement check, and an import/export loss ledger.
bridge_ideas.evidence: 568/568 Blender X3D 4.0 re-exports are valid on fork d5598c4 and upstream 74da0ec, including 211 inputs the fork rated invalid (val/exp_*.jsonl). Y8: first-try-valid scenes are complete 71.8% of the time, after one repair 61.8%, after two 38.5%; two judges agree 92%, kappa 0.82 (fork d5598c4, X_ITE 16.5.0).

bridge_ideas.idea: Benchmark design for the missing Blender-vs-x3d_mcp comparison: reuse the E1 harness and prompts-v1.jsonl, restricted to the 115 licence-clean prompts whose nodes Blender can express (85 library + 18 bench30 + 12 unseen31). Arm A is the existing x3d-text arm, arm B is model-writes-bpy then x3d-blender-io export. Same validators, same X_ITE render check, same judge. Arm A baselines for the subset need a BigQuery read of e1_verdicts.
bridge_ideas.evidence: prompts-v1.jsonl: 300 prompts; 138 of 239 library prompts and 113 of 230 exemplar slots come from veiled scenes, so a shareable benchmark must drop them; 30 of 61 hand-written prompts need only importer-handled nodes (18/30, 12/31). E1 x3d-text arm (fork d5598c4, X_ITE 16.5.0): flash 27.3->56.7%, gpt-6.1-sol 64->86.7%, argon 18.7->50% first-try valid without/with 2 exemplars.

bridge_ideas.idea: Round-trip fixture tiers from the corpus: Tier A (111 clean valid RT-stable distinct node-sets, list in scratch), Tier B (44 distinct node-sets of fork-valid scenes with unhandled nodes, as expected-loss cases), Tier C (regenerated mutants), Tier D (natural broken files; only 16 on disk, the 668 clean tuned-eval ones need the GCS tarballs). Pass criteria: no exception, validator-clean re-export, faces/bbox/objects/materials stable.
bridge_ideas.evidence: Of 568 imported clean scenes, 531 (93.5%) keep faces, bbox, object count and material count after Blender-> X3D 4.0 -> Blender; 393/409 (96.1%) of scenes with only importer-handled nodes versus 138/159 (86.8%) with unhandled nodes. 316 scenes show a higher vertex count only because the exporter splits vertices per UV/normal.

bridge_ideas.idea: Split GaussianSplats nodes into slabs of at most ~40-50k splats in the exporter (as trailer make_presets_depth.py does) and add huge_tree=True to x3d_mcp validate.py. The first removes the libxml2 10 MB start-tag limit, the second removes the false XSD failure and slabs also help X_ITE ordering.
bridge_ideas.evidence: Clean 140,000-splat scene: original 12.26 MB and the Blender 4.1 re-export 11.29 MB both fail XSD on 688174f, d5598c4, 74da0ec and fork main 8dd0d3e ('Buffer size limit exceeded, try XML_PARSE_HUGE', line 16 col 10,002,914); trailer note: 80,000-splat start tag 11.87 MB, 50,000-splat nodes about 7.4 MB validate. Blender import/export of the same file is exact.

bridge_ideas.idea: Licence passport on Blender exports: write creator, licence, generator version and source-scene sha256 into the head meta by default, and teach the spine classifier GPL/LGPL/Unlicense and treat CC BY-ND as restricted for derivatives. That lets Blender-made files enter the spine as 'converted' lineage rows and be clean.
bridge_ideas.evidence: collect.py regexes run on exporter strings: 'GNU GPL v3', 'GNU LGPL v3', 'Unlicense', 'NONE' -> unknown (veiled); 'CC BY-ND 4.0' -> permissive. The x3d-blender-io splats-fixture-x3d41.x3d carries meta license NONE and is veiled (snapshot id 6c1acb7c, licence unknown); all 11 blender_export scenes are veiled. Exporter enum has CC_BY_4.0, CC0_1.0, GPL_v3, LGPL_v3 (source/__init__.py:388+).

bridge_ideas.idea: Importer 'loss ledger': after import, store a per-scene report of node types skipped, flattened or approximated (seeded from the measured survival table), so Blender users and agents see what was dropped.

bridge_ideas.idea: Prioritise importer node support by corpus frequency: ColorInterpolator -> material colour fcurve (43 clean scenes, 6 clean-lit), GeoLocation/GeoViewpoint/GeoOrigin -> local offset plus camera (159/140/18 clean scenes), then Script/Touch/ProximitySensor as inert custom-property stubs. Science-viz coverage is nil: no clean valid PointSet, ColorRGBA, MetadataFloat or volume scenes, and splats are 5 clean scenes at SH0 only. The splat-first scope must lean on synthetic PLY fixtures and the trailer pipeline (20,000-splat bit-exact export per HALL.md), not on the spine; SH>=1 colour and Blender 5.3 native PointClouds are untested here (bpy 5.2.3 only, mesh fallback).

Licence-clean is narrower than it sounds: 2,153 of 2,205 are our own model outputs classed by kind, not by content, with provider terms for using frontier-model outputs untested (Suspected); only 52 are explicitly permissive (CC BY needs attribution). 377 veiled scenes look like our own authored files (showcase, hand, blender_export) and could be promoted only by HagopJay's typed attestation; I did not promote or use them.
The brief for Dr. Polys says '3,058 public X3D scenes'; only 474 come from a public mirror, 52 carry explicit licences. Fix the wording before any send (nothing is to leave without his typed 'send').

A v3 blind set is still owed.

digests.summary: The Polyxandria Hall build is a 3,058-scene X3D spine rendered two ways: X_ITE headless (tools/shoot.mjs) and Blender Cycles through x3d-blender-io (src/cycles_hall.py, src/freeze_x3d.py, tools/cube_colour.py, tools/never_black.py). HALL.md records that the engines agree on geometry but not on look: lit AgX R/B is 1.17-1.18 vs X_ITE 1.23, the waiting wall R/B is 0.781 vs 0.718, and bridge pin 5da2707 vs main 342c8c5 differs by 26.4 dB with a pink horizon. I re-ran the key claims hands-on on bpy 5.2.3 LTS (Cycles CPU) and X_ITE 16.5.0 and 16.5.1 headless (SwiftShader). The pink horizon reproduces bit-exactly (99 dB against the stored 5.2.2 render) and is caused by PR #19 restoring the sun-glow Rectangle2D emissive colour, plus 4 Disk2D/Rectangle2D objects imported since d87fa8c. A purpose-built 8-row x 12-patch colour chart shows Blender's Khronos PBR Neutral view transform matches X_ITE's KHR_PBR_NEUTRAL for lit PBR (mean error 2.5-3.6 levels of 255 vs 12 for AgX Medium High Contrast). The same chart shows the importer treats UnlitMaterial, legacy Material and Background in the wrong colour space or not at all, and that point and spot energy is about 7.2x too dim for X_ITE's physical model. X_ITE 16.5.0 and 16.5.1 were pixel-identical on every fixture I rendered, so the '16.5.0 blank in some cases' cause is not the rendering path (likely IMPORT/EXPORT or Inline handling; Suspected). On the validator side, none of fork 688174f, upstream 74da0ec or main 8dd0d3e checks lights, visibility, sort order or unlit colour: my valid-but-invisible fixtures all pass XSD and semantic checks while X_ITE draws them blank or wrong. The 10 MB XSD start-tag limit on large GaussianSplats also persists on all three, and a one-line huge_tree change clears it in scratch.

offers_to_blender: A measured look-parity recipe: Blender's Khronos PBR Neutral view transform reproduces X_ITE KHR_PBR_NEUTRAL for lit PBR (mean error 2.5-3.6 levels vs 11.8-12.5 for AgX Medium High Contrast and 13-17 for Standard), with AgX remaining the beauty choice.

Three importer fixes with working prototypes in src/bl_fix.py: sRGB-to-linear for UnlitMaterial emissiveColor and legacy colours (unlit rows go from 35-46 mean error to 0.0-0.2 under Standard), camera-ray-only world from the x3d_background custom property (Background 0.2 0.4 0.6 renders 51,102,153 exactly instead of black), and point/spot energy 4*pi*I W (57/112/210/255 vs X_ITE 58/110/206/255, importer currently 17/41/85/161).

An X_ITE-exact animation evaluator (freeze_x3d.py) to extend or test the importer ROUTE coverage, which today animates only Transform translation/rotation/scale, HAnimJoint and CoordinateInterpolator point shape keys.

A regression fixture set (chart2, alpha, plight, sorthaz, anim/film, huge splats) that gives look-parity numbers rather than only structural round-trip checks, complementing the in-flight PR #24 export suite.
Evidence that the dawn-hide workaround in cycles_hall.py is obsolete on main: with PR #20 the orange dawn band draws (left band mean 44,32,25 vs X_ITE 34,27,31).
Blender sees the transparent-sort hazard as a non-issue (Cycles draws the glow regardless), which makes Cycles a useful oracle for 'what the author meant' vs X_ITE's drawn result.
offers_to_x3d: A tested list of valid-but-invisible cases the three validator commits do not catch: no light with headlight false and a lit material (renders 0,0,0), Viewpoint with nothing in the frustum (blank), UnlitMaterial emissive black with no texture (0,0,0), missing texture file (draws untextured with 2 console errors), metallic PhysicalMaterial without environment light (renders near-white), and a transparent Shape whose bboxCenter/bboxSize pulls it behind the sky in X_ITE's sort.

X_ITE 16.5.0 rendering rules read from dist/x_ite.js: GAMMA 2.2 pure power, ColorSpace default LINEAR_WHEN_PHYSICAL_MATERIAL, unlit and legacy Material in sRGB numbers with no decode, transparent shapes sorted far-to-near by view-space bbox centre z with depthMask false, MaxLights 8 (2 when MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS is 8 or less), OrderIndependentTransparency page option.

A one-line validator fix: pass XMLParser(huge_tree=True, resolve_entities=False, no_network=True) in validate_xml so XSD validation accepts GaussianSplats start tags over about 10,000,000 bytes (fails at 10.56 MB SH1 and 10.72 MB SH3 on all three commits).
A per-node splat size table from the emitter: about 154.6 / 257.7 / 429.6 / 670.2 bytes per splat for SH0/1/2/3, giving max about 64.7k / 38.8k / 23.3k / 14.9k splats per node under the 10 MB limit.

Blank-render statistics from the Hall: glass 'mirror' scenes (valid on both validators, nonblank_ratio below 0.002 in all views) are 112 plus 81 veiled = 193 of 957 lit scenes (20.2%, X_ITE 16.5.0 cached view 0), a ready denominator for a blank-render gate using analyze_frame.
Pinned-validator comparison harness (src/val_one.py, sem_report.py) running fork 688174f, upstream 74da0ec and main 8dd0d3e on the same file.

Warm lit R/B reproduces the Hall gap: amber 1.524 (X_ITE) vs 1.545 (Khronos) vs 1.471 (AgX MHC); sun colour 2.938 vs 3.124 vs 2.674.

bridge_ideas.idea: Convert UnlitMaterial emissiveColor and legacy Material colours from X3D numbers to linear (piecewise EOTF) on import, as an option, because X_ITE shows them as sRGB numbers.
bridge_ideas.evidence: bl_fix.py unlit mode: rows A and B go to mean error 0.2 / 0.0 (max 1) vs X_ITE under Standard; unmodified, unlit 0.5 gives Blender 188 vs X_ITE 128. Whether the X3D spec intends sRGB numbers for legacy colours is not settled here, so the fix is a look-parity option rather than a spec claim.

Parity (Khronos PBR Neutral) conflicts with beauty (AgX): Neutral matches X_ITE but crushes darks, so the importer can only offer parity as an option, not a default; HagopJay's 'highest visual fidelity' goal must pick which target counts.

digests.slice: splat-trailer: Cycles -> gsplat MCMC -> X3D 4.1 GaussianSplats -> X_ITE path (Anamnesis trailer v1..v3.1, Marble/Pantheon, Splat Park) plus hands-on round-trip, validator-wall, ordering and oracle tests on bpy 5.2.3 LTS
digests.summary: The Library's Anamnesis trailer is a complete, logged, Blender-to-X3D splat pipeline. Hall v1_8b is rendered in Cycles (bpy 5.2.2 OptiX, 300 views, AgX +1.50, alpha), trained with gsplat 1.5.3 MCMC to 1,000,000 splats (held-out 30.84 / 27.10 / 27.42 dB for v1/v2/v3), exported through the x3d-blender-io bridge as float32-exact X3D 4.1, re-chunked into depth-slab nodes, validated on fork 688174f and upstream 74da0ec (0 errors), and drawn by X_ITE 16.5.0 (pixel-identical to 16.5.1). Three X_ITE/libxml2 traps drive the file layout: nodes are sorted as transparent shapes by bbox centre (19.06 dB file-order vs 26.35 dB slabs), a start tag over 10,000,000 bytes is refused by the stock XSD parser (25k splats/node at SH1), and a frustum-culled node never sorts so loadURL hangs. I reproduced all three on a 3,125-splat fixture, plus new findings: the exporter writes one un-chunked node with no bbox, so real scenes fail the fork XSD; X_ITE culls splats whose footprint exceeds min(viewport); X_ITE reads PLY and glTF KHR_gaussian_splatting but no SPZ/SOG. PLY -> Blender 5.2.3 (mesh and native-layout PointCloud, FLOAT4 works) -> X3D 4.1 -> Blender -> PLY is float32-exact at SH0-3 on synthetic and real (323,295-splat Sphinx) data; a numpy oracle matches X_ITE at 46-52 dB for SH0-SH3, which gives a renderer-independent metric that catches the valid-but-wrong classes the validators miss (node order, quaternion order). Blender 5.3 native-splat facts remain Likely (no 5.3 build or blender/blender read access here); a ready probe script settles seven open layout questions in one run.

offers_to_blender: Ground-truth views: Cycles (bpy 5.2.2 OptiX, 128 spp max, adaptive 0.01, OIDN, film_transparent, AgX MHC +1.50) is the only renderer the splats are trained from; the sweep script and nerfstudio transforms writer are reusable for any Blender scene.

A tested PLY/X3D splat path on 5.2 LTS: splat_io + mesh fallback and the native-layout PointCloud (FLOAT4 radiance:base, resize) both round-trip float32-exact on bpy 5.2.3 at SH0-3, so 5.3 behaviour can be diffed against a known-good 5.2 baseline.

Chunking and bbox logic (make_presets_depth/walk) to add to the exporter so any Blender splat object leaves as validator-clean, X_ITE-correct X3D (today it leaves as one node, 154.5 B/splat SH0, over the wall at about 65k).
Validator and X_ITE as an acceptance gate for Blender splat scripts: fork XSD + semantic reports and the oracle PSNR close the Blender lane's missing guard for splat work.
Metric kit: held-out PSNR over black/white, alpha MAE, per-view eval_views, match_check (channel means within 2, PSNR >= 30), plus my oracle + cull emulation, usable on any Blender-produced splat.

Colour rule to carry into any 5.3 splat viewing: Anamnesis splats are trained on AgX display-referred frames, so Blender must view them with Standard (AgX would tone-map twice); X_ITE draws them untoned.
Real-data corpus: Sphinx (323k), planet-scale (453k), Pantheon + 5 Marble worlds (500k SPZ), synthsplat (133k, SH3) as inputs for 5.3 importer tests.
offers_to_x3d: Fixture ladder S0-S3 (3,125 splats, deterministic) with expected-loss table and oracle PSNR floor 45 dB; X_ITE 16.5.0, 16.5.1 and 16.6.0 produce byte-identical PNGs on it.

Candidate validator rules (propose to the Playground thread, do not build here): splat-start-tag-size (warn above about 9.5 MB: 64,000 SH0 pass, 66,000 fail on fork main), splat-node-order (nodes with near-equal bbox centres and heavy overlap: 8 file-order nodes score centre-distance 0.031 / IoU 0.84, slabs 0.131 / 0.40, cells 0.33 / 0.005), and a note that quaternion order cannot be caught by the heuristic on rotated scenes.

Evidence for upstream notes held until 'send': splat node sort by bbox centre, the frustum-cull loadURL hang on 16.5.0/16.5.1/16.6.0, the min(viewport) quad cull, no SPZ/SOG loader in the 16.6.0 npm bundle, and the unstated x y z w order (SFQuaternion is a bare 4-tuple).

Proof of render-based checking: three valid-but-wrong cases the validators pass with 0 warnings (node order 19.7-22.4 dB, w-first quaternions 27.1-29.3 dB, near-splat cull 18.7 dB vs 49.5 dB oracle-with-cull) that a renderer-independent PSNR separates cleanly.

Per-node capacity table from measured bytes: 154.5 / 264.5 / 448 / 705 B of start tag per splat for SH0-3 gives about 64.7k / 37.8k / 22.3k / 14.2k splats per node under 10,000,000 B (predicted for SH2-3).

bridge_ideas.idea: Splat round-trip fixture ladder (RT-S0..S3 synthetic + R1..R5 real). Chain PLY -> X3D 4.1 -> Blender (5.2 mesh, 5.2 native-layout PointCloud, 5.3 native) -> X3D -> PLY, then SPZ (5.3 import) and glTF KHR. Metrics: M1 PLY->X3D max abs diff 0 ulp (float32-exact); M2 X3D->Blender->X3D 0 ulp; M3 Blender->PLY: xyz/f_dc/f_rest 0, ln-scale <= 6e-8, quaternion (sign-free) <= 6e-8, opacity judged in alpha space (<= 1e-6, logit clamps at +-13.8155); M4 fork XSD + semantic 0 errors, upstream 0 errors; M5 oracle PSNR vs X_ITE >= 45 dB at 3 poses per SH degree; M6 bytes/splat table; M7 load time and peak RSS.
bridge_ideas.evidence: M1-M3 measured on bpy 5.2.3 + add-on 2.6.4 (482741b), synthetic N=2000 (rt_2000.json) and real Sphinx N=323,295 (real_sphinx_*.json): all exact, alpha max error 9.9e-7, 33,612 of 323,295 real splats (10.4%) have logit > 13.8155. M5: 46.17-51.69 dB measured (fx3, fx2).

bridge_ideas.idea: Exporter option 'max bytes per GaussianSplats node' with spatial-cell (walk) and depth-slab (shot) modes and bbox fields, ported from make_presets_depth/walk, so Blender-exported splats are validator-clean and X_ITE-ordered by default; default cell mode with cull-off bbox to avoid the load hang.

digests.summary: The slice is a private exhibit shelf of real, mostly validated X3D. It has 6 Marble splat worlds (5 x 500,000 splats plus an 84-splat stub) plus the Pantheon as X3D 4.1 (.x3dz). It has Giza (plateau X3D 4.0, Khufu to 1,675,819 splats, trained Sphinx today/restored splats), a synthetic Hegra stand-in, and Blender-origin PBR fixtures. It also has the Cycles-vs-X_ITE "bridge" still life, the Blacksburg lidar twin, the planet-scale zoom and a Material Odyssey film. Nine bpy scripts already exist as Blender-side recipes (bridge/build.py, synthsplat and Sphinx render+export, planet-scale render_dsm/export). Nothing in /mnt/project-files is volumetric, molecular or medical: there are no PDB, mmCIF, DICOM, NIfTI, NetCDF, HDF5, LAS or EXR files and no X3D volume nodes except probe templates. Hall II ("Seeing the Body") is a 2-joint HAnim arm, and Hall IV ("CAVE") is a panorama plus a solar system. Hands-on this session (bpy 5.2.3 LTS, x3d-blender-io main 482741b, fork validator main eb4b4b4, no browser so no X_ITE): all four 500k and 50k splat X3D masters I tried import into Blender in about 9 s (0.7 s for 50k), and every non-500k file passes XSD, semantic and profile checks. Four new defects surfaced: a per-vertex Color double sRGB decode on import (one-line fix verified in a scratch copy), an exporter that writes linear colour verbatim, Marble scene.json scale/translation dropped from all six X3D masters, and a 500k-splat XSD-4.1 "Internal error" that leaves the heritage worlds unchecked at XSD level. Hall mapping: I Early Web = interchange fixtures; II Body = medical volumes + molecular, which is empty; III Agents = agent lane / simulation; IV CAVE = cameras/panoramic/astronomy; V Heritage = splats + LiDAR/geoscience, which is the richest hall. Best Blender-owned look sources are the bridge still life and the Sphinx. Best X3D-native imports are the Marble/Pantheon/Khufu splat worlds and the earth-twin and planet-scale terrain. A sci-vis hall can be populated today with the splat worlds, the Sphinx era pair, the earth-twin and the exporter fixtures. Hall II needs new volume and molecule exhibits, for which only a volume feasibility demo and recipe exist (outside this slice).

digests.summary: The fork is a mature, tested X3D 4.0/4.1 bridge for Blender, and splats are its strongest sci-vis path. Main is 482741b (merge of PR #24). All 24 PRs are merged except open PR #25 (hagsmac, bulk attribute reads), and there are 0 issues. On bpy 5.2.3 LTS the full unit suite passes 145/145 (57 of them run without bpy), and the 194-case export conformance suite passes CORE 147/147. Hands-on splat round trips (PLY to X3D 4.1 to Blender to PLY, 5,000 and 100,000 splats, SH0 and SH3, mesh and native-layout PointCloud targets) are exact to 3e-8 in linear units. Positions and SH coefficients are bit-exact. The one measured loss is opacity logits beyond about +-13.8, which splat_io clamps. Everything outside splats, ordinary meshes, PBR, HAnim, Inline and shape-key morphs is thin for scientific visualization. Colour data is the worst: vertex colours are double gamma-converted on import, never made the active colour, and so vanish on the next export. PointSet and IndexedLineSet colour is ignored, and a vertex-only mesh or PointCloud cannot be exported. CoordinateDouble, Geo*, Volume* and Metadata outside a Shape, plus head units, are dropped. Of the 15 Oct memo losses, only Background is fixed. Normal is a default-off export option rather than a loss. ColorRGBA, UnlitMaterial identity and Transform/instance structure still lose data. A check of the x3d_mcp validator fork (integration/validator-fixes, tip acdf5c4) found that its XSD path rejects any splat file whose GaussianSplats start tag reaches about 10 MB, while its semantic path already uses huge_tree. No X_ITE render was run in this slice, so X_ITE patch claims here are second-hand.

digests.summary: The fork at main 8dd0d3e (still the head on 25 Oct) is a 35-tool, 4-prompt, 0-resource MCP server whose Layer-4 semantic checker emits 36 check ids (semantic.py, 1,092 lines), with 481 tests passing (my rerun, Python 3.13.17). Its 8 splat checks cover only encoding-space and array-length mistakes (ln-scale, logit-opacity, quaternion order, SH-degree gaps); nothing checks colour range of SH0, visibility, scale against extent, units, 32-bit precision, Color/Normal counts, metadata ranges or volumes. The Playground thread's plan (review-2026-10-24: gauntlet G0-G8, 10 ranked skills of which 3 are written, 13 'Break it' operators) has no science-visualisation item: grep of review-results.json finds 0 hits for pLDDT, SH0, view transform or colour management, and 'UNIT' once as 'unmeasured'. I therefore built, as scratch only, a trailer-free patch (9 check functions, 12 ids, 15 tests, applies cleanly to 8dd0d3e, suite 496 passed) plus 23 probe scenes, real-scene mutants, a project-drive false-alarm scan and a two-phase Blender-script guard. On 23 probes, 8 are already caught by the XSD, and 13 are XSD-valid defects that main calls clean; the patch flags 10 of 13 and 0 of 2 controls. On 24 splat and 51 normal mutants of real scenes main flags none; the patch fires 17/24 and 51/51, and 0 findings on 1,720 parseable project-drive scenes. The guard (bpy 5.2.3 + x3d-blender-io 482741b + fork 8dd0d3e) runs in 3.2 s, stopped a bad agent script (3 of 5 planted mistakes caught) and passed a good one. Calibration is thin: 12 unique real splat clouds, 0 real pLDDT, 0 VolumeData, 0 <unit>, 0 CoordinateDouble scenes on the project drive. pLDDT and volume rules rest on synthetic probes only; thresholds (SH0 non-negative test, 1/255, 1000 float32 steps) are heuristics and the first real dataset may move them. Zero findings in the scan is not evidence the corpus is defect-free.

Severity choices are mine: volume-no-voxels as error (spec default is NULL), plddt-range error at or above 100, attribute-count error. The pLDDT metadata naming is a convention, not part of X3D; it needs the registry and agreement before it gates anything. The AFDB 70 band is not in the KB (Suspected).

Weak spots measured: splat-scale-huge caught the double-exp mutant in 1 of 6 scenes; UTM offset in 4 of 6; the spacing-based rule is calibrated but not implemented; P18 and P19 are not caught; the guard missed 2 of 5 planted mistakes (0..1 ramp for a 0..100 value, Emission Strength).

digests.summary: x3d.ML (private, main 5379a80, PRs #1-#5 merged; branch claude/x3d-traceability-rwrcnn is still advancing with Firehose 4, no PR) holds x3dprov: a SHA-256 hash chain written as x3dprov.version and x3dprov.step.N head metas inside the scene, with verify() returning verified, stale, broken-chain or no-record. That is the in-file provenance carrier, and ML-pipeline traceability is HagopJay's idea. I reproduced the key hooks hands-on on bpy 5.2.3 LTS (build e13b728c6880) with x3d-blender-io main 482741b and x3d_mcp fork main 8dd0d3e (XSD only). Head metas and the chain survive the Blender import and export; an unrecorded round trip reads stale and a recorded transform step reads verified. A Cycles render can carry the chain head in the EXR header and PNG text chunks through scene.render.stamp_note_text, and the chain can record the figure back with a render step of about 1 KB. The same hands-on work found sharp edges. Shape-level MetadataSet survives but Transform, Group, Material, geometry, WorldInfo and GaussianSplats metadata do not. A faceless PointSet mesh is dropped along with its MetadataSet. Two stamped files imported into one scene break the chain. Text splat scenes of 100k splats or more cannot be parsed by the fork, and x3dprov silently falls back to a text hash at the same size. For compact encodings I built the missing PLY/SPZ/SOG/X3D-text table for the 132,923-splat trained set at SH0-SH3. SPZ gives 4.4x to 12.2x over PLY, SOG gives 5.5x and 5.8x at SH0 and SH1 (SH2 and SH3 timed out on CPU), and the add-on's current text is far larger than the 17 Oct table assumed. The ecosystem watch (stale since 12 Oct, routine reportedly paused) still works. Re-run in scratch it flagged 11 changes (bpy 5.2.3, X_ITE 16.6.0, splat-transform 3.10.3 and others) and has no probes for the sci-vis items on the KB re-check list. A primary-source read of KhronosGroup/glTF upgrades KHR_gaussian_splatting to ratified. X_ITE 16.6.0 contains Draco, meshopt and KTX decoders but no SPZ or SOG path.

offers_to_blender: A provenance recipe for any Blender-rendered figure, confirmed on bpy 5.2.3 with Cycles CPU. Set scene.render.use_stamp_note=True and stamp_note_text to the x3dprov chain head, plus script sha256, bpy version and build hash, engine, samples and view transform. The Note lands in the EXR header (Note, Software, colorInteropID=lin_rec709_scene, cycles.ViewLayer.*) and in the PNG tEXt chunk. The chain then gets a render step (about 1,067 B) carrying the pixel hash and the embedded head.
The chain lives in Blender as scene['x3d_head_meta'] (a list of {name, content}); it persists in a saved .blend and reloads (t8), so a .blend, its X3D export and its figure share one record.

Verification guard for agent-written scripts (KB section 7): after any script run P.verify(exported_x3d) and treat stale or broken-chain as a failed step. This closes the Blender lane's missing guard without a model call; validate_xml (XSD) is about 1 ms to 4 s depending on size.

Measured size table for choosing a splat format at SH0-SH3 (hard_facts): SPZ is the best general choice, SOG wins at SH0 only, and X3D text + brotli-11 only matches raw PLY, so text splats are for fixtures, not delivery.

Version register backed by a runnable probe: bpy 5.2.3 (22 Oct) is now the LTS wheel, Molecular Nodes tag v520.2.0 and PyPI molecularnodes 520.2.0 (18 Sep) match the KB, Microscopy Nodes v3.1.3, Bioxel Nodes v2.0.4, LichtFeld v0.5.4.2, usd-core 26.11 (21 Oct), openexr 3.5.2 (3 Oct) can be watched with the existing probe types.

Primary-source facts for splat work: KHR_gaussian_splatting is 'Complete, Ratified by the Khronos Group'; its colorSpace values are ColorInterop IDs (srgb_rec709_display, lin_rec709_display), the same vocabulary as Blender 5.x EXR colorInteropID and X3D GaussianSplats colorSpace.

Hygiene warnings from the render test: stamp Hostname and Date are on by default in the flags I set and 'Hostname: vm' lands in EXR and PNG; turn use_stamp_hostname and use_stamp_date off for any shared figure. Hash pixels, not file bytes (cycles.ViewLayer.total_time makes identical renders differ byte-wise).
offers_to_x3d: A science-figure profile for x3dprov that needs no change to x3dprov.py (add_step takes any dict): ingest with data_sha256, bytes, accession and licence; script with script_sha256; render with engine, samples, seed, device, view_transform, colorInteropID, bpy version and build, pixel_sha256, embedded_chain_head. A worked 4-step example verifies on bpy 5.2.3 (out_t4/scene_with_render_step.x3d).

Concrete bugs and behaviours for x3d-blender-io (482741b), each reproduced: faceless point-cloud meshes are not exported (extract.py:1060, only an info meta), taking the Shape's MetadataSet with them; node Metadata survives only on Shape; two stamped imports into one scene duplicate x3dprov.step.N and break the chain; bl_info version (2,6,1) in source/__init__.py:9 vs manifest 2.6.4, so the exported generator meta is wrong.

Text-splat ceiling facts that support the standards ask for a binary or URL splat payload: fork validate_xml accepts 75,000 splats (9.9 MB) and rejects 100,000 (13.2 MB) with the libxml2 10 MB cap at 8dd0d3e, and X_ITE 16.6.0 has no SPZ, SOG or compressed-PLY path though it ships Draco, meshopt and KTX decoders. Private until 'send'.

Hash-method gap in x3dprov for the maintainers' next version: record a hash_method field (c14n or text-fallback) and an assets[] list (sidecar sha256, bytes, codec) so SPZ/SOG/EXR sidecars are pinned by the chain.

bridge_ideas.idea: Figure-to-chain binding for Blender renders: write the chain head (sha256 of the last x3dprov step JSON) into scene.render.stamp_note_text in a render_pre handler; after rendering, a render_post/render_write handler computes sha256 of the float pixels and appends a render step whose prev equals the embedded head. The image then points to the chain and the chain points to the image (both directions checked).
bridge_ideas.evidence: t4_render_stamp.py on bpy 5.2.3 e13b728c6880: EXR header and PNG tEXt both carry Note with the head; chain with render step verifies (status verified, 4 steps); render step prev == embedded head: true; handlers render_pre, render_post, render_write, render_complete, save_post exist in bpy.app.handlers. x3dprov.add_step accepts arbitrary step dicts (x3dprov.py).

bridge_ideas.idea: Hash pixels, not bytes, for figure identity: Cycles CPU with seed 0 gives identical float pixels for identical scenes while EXR files differ in one header attribute (cycles.ViewLayer.total_time). Use pixel_sha256 (and optionally strip the cycles.ViewLayer.*_time attrs) in the render step; keep PNG/JPEG out of /mnt/project-files because the host's C2PA stamping rewrites bytes within about 15 s.

digests.summary: HagopJay's stated priorities, in order (MEMORY.md): (1) the AI flywheel, "improve how to improve" through A/B comparisons that surface emergent features, hub = University-scale thread, loop defined in research/university-scale-2026-10-17/flywheel/FLYWHEEL-LEDGER.md (model writes, exact validator, real render, judge consensus, Blender owns the look, failures become rules); (2) the tether, "X3D is the 3D format an AI can be held accountable to", valid is not visible, name the validator commit; (3) stack rule: X3D master, Blender owns the look, every Blender scene also exports validated X3D, Unreal rising (Shroud eventually), Castle converts X3D to glTF (his word, unmeasured); (4) twins Shroud > Giza > Burruss, plus the Library of PolyXandria as the Dr. Polys-facing gift. Doha (13-15 Oct) outcome is still unreported, email v2 is his to send, nothing leaves without typed "send", and Blender-as-essential-AI-3D-tool and x3d-blender-io-to-full-spec are his ideas. The Blender sci-vis expert is the "look and measure" organ of flywheel step 5 and a supplier of exact oracles to steps 3-4 (exactness ladder proven > computed > judged), as reviewer/spec-writer rather than builder; the library is at once the corpus (3,058 spine scenes: 957 lit, 1,835 dark, 260 split, 4 unread/2 undecidable), a calibration instrument (Hall Cycles-vs-X_ITE colour and PSNR numbers, Anamnesis Cycles -> gsplat -> X3D 4.1 -> X_ITE) and the showcase. Measured here (Confirmed, snapshot_v1.jsonl): the library is rich in failure breadth but nearly empty of sci-vis content (0 lit scenes with Metadata nodes, 1 volume scene, 23 splat scenes, only 4 licence-clean lit archive scenes), so Blender must manufacture the sci-vis fixtures; that is the one thing the library cannot supply and the clearest two-way trade. The loop has already turned: four x3d-blender-io PRs (#17-#20) came from Hall render defects, and Blender-origin scenes tripped the fork profile check (5 of 11 split), which led to the Shape level-2 component fix. What is missing is instrumentation: no per-hop metric, no corpus-wide round-trip harness, no Blender-agent benchmark, and the splat round-trip fixture pack from the v1.1 addendum is still unrun. Horizons: NOW (to Blender 5.3 on 10 Nov 2026) splat round-trip fixture pack on bpy 5.2.3 with expected-loss table plus re-validation of the 11 Blender-origin scenes; 3 MONTHS (to the 1 Jan 2027 Enrie unlock) corpus-wide round-trip harness, agent A/B, Castle/Blender-to-Unreal bake-off, calibrated render-pair judge set; 1 YEAR a conformance-and-fidelity suite any X3D exporter can run, with evidence-backed spec asks, offered through Dr. Polys after "send". Dr. Polys and the Web3D community would most value exact evidence (named validator commits, 0 false alarms), reusable fixtures, a working modern Blender X3D path (upstream io_scene_x3d 2.5.1 is 19 months stale), and sharp spec questions, none of it sent yet. Main risk: the validator of record is unsettled (688174f/d5598c4/eb4b4b4/8dd0d3e), so every metric must pin its commit.

digests.summary: The ontology slice (X3D Ontology 4.1 Turtle, 18,121 triples, 364 classes; X3DUOM 4.1) is already a working lookup layer: it predicts 348 legal parent/child pairs of which XSD 4.1 accepts 150, rejects 163 and leaves 35 inconclusive (fork validator eb4b4b4), and the wrong-type USE check finds 96/96 injected faults with 0 false alarms on 200 archive scenes. This session built the Blender side of the bridge, hands-on on bpy 5.2.3: a sci-vis Blender scene exported by x3d-blender-io 482741b (v2.6.1) to X3D (27,828 B), converted to Turtle (7,004 triples), checked with SHACL (pyshacl 0.40.1) and written back to Blender as bone/object properties, closing the loop Blender to X3D to Turtle to SHACL to Blender. The ontology can consume from Blender: hierarchy, materials, x3d_metadata/head meta, bone names (to HAnimJoint). It can give back: semantic labels, HAnim joint validation (joint name, parent, LOA, rest centre from X3DUOM), and UOM/quantity/provenance metadata. The importer has real gaps that matter to sci-vis fidelity: UNIT is neither emitted nor read, collections are flattened, and default-value handling is wrong for Sphere (radius 0.5 instead of 1), UnlitMaterial (emissive imports black, not 1 1 1) and PhysicalMaterial (baseColor imports 0.8 grey, not 1 1 1). Blender is a usable exact-geometry oracle for the step-4 contact check: with the Sphere default corrected in a scratch importer copy it agrees with the AABB check on 34 of 34 gpt-4o 'cube on sphere' scenes (15 rest, 16 sunk, 3 gap), while on constructed scenes the AABB check gives false contacts that exact BVH rejects. For the Hall/library, the full hall_v1_7.x3d to Turtle is 4,369,498 triples because of RDF-list array encoding, but array elision brings it to 12,473 triples, and the snapshot_v1 spine graph is 222,163 triples and queryable. digests.summary: Compression slice. The 17 Oct compact-encodings thread (README-v2.md) measured everything on fork main cf84f64, a descendant of 688174f, eb4b4b4 and 74da0ec but not of d5598c4. Its headline: lossless re-encoding gains almost nothing once a long-window compressor runs, and lossy quantization is the lever. Brotli-11 shrinks ten Shroud X3D scenes 28,988,973 B to 907,529 B (32x), against 5.7x for the gzip inside .x3dz. Float32 glTF plus brotli equals X3D text plus brotli within 2.3%. Draco or meshopt plus brotli is about 3x smaller than text plus brotli on those scenes. For splats, text plus brotli lands within 7 to 27% of a shipped SPZ on already-quantized Marble worlds. On a trained SH3 set, an SPZ-style stream is 8.5x smaller than the best text. I reproduced the key numbers today and added three new hands-on results. (1) The 10 MB libxml2 start-tag wall is still live on fork main 8dd0d3e (Oct 18, descendant of cf84f64, not of d5598c4), and the current x3d-blender-io exporter now writes float32-exact text, which puts the wall at about 14,000 splats at SH3. (2) That same exporter's SH3 .x3dz is bigger than the PLY it came from. (3) A fidelity harness (my own C rasterizer, PSNR and SSIM against uncompressed) shows an SPZ-style codec costs about 38.3 dB at SH3, and the loss comes from DC colour clipping and SH bit-drop, not geometry. Still open: bpy 5.2.3 pip has no Draco or meshopt bridge (the export flags are silently ignored), AB-RESULTS.md and HANDOFF.md are missing from disk, and no X_ITE-vs-Cycles PSNR before/after has been run. Nothing was written to the project, sent or pushed, and I made no commits.

Blender splat PLY/SPZ size arithmetic: PLY = 62 float32 per splat at SH3 (x,y,z, 3 normals, 3 f_dc, 45 f_rest, opacity, 3 scale, 4 rot) = 248 B, SH0 17 floats = 68 B, SH1 104 B, SH2 164 B; checks: synthsplat 1,531 header + 132,923 x 248 = 32,966,435; Pantheon 500,000 x 68 + 416 = 34,000,416 B. KB v1 sec 4 says '59 numbers, 248 bytes': the 248 B counts 3 unused normals, 59 numbers excludes them (59 x 4 = 236). SPZ v3 stream = 16 B header + 20 B/splat at SH0 (9 pos + 1 alpha + 3 colour + 3 scale + 4 rotation), +9/+24/+45 B for SH1/2/3 = 65 B at SH3: 10,000,016 B for 500k SH0 and 8,640,011 B for 132,923 SH3.

huge_tree trade-off: it lifts libxml2's guard against oversized text from untrusted input. semantic.py:1020 already enables it unbounded (entities unresolved, no network) while validate.py does not, so the two layers disagree on large scenes; a bounded setting (explicit size cap, e.g. 256 MB) needs HagopJay's decision. Above about 13.5 MB per attribute even huge_tree hits the XSD engine's internal error, so lifting the cap does not solve scale; slabbing does for text, a binary/URL payload does for the standard.

Rules for the public fork hagopjay/x3d_mcp (public): no AI trailers or Co-Authored-By/Claude-Session lines in any commit or PR text proposed for it (CONTRIBUTING.md:28, human authorship only); no vendor/model names, project id or cost figures; one PR per fix, issue first; patches go via the trailer-free kit research/x3d_mcp-patches/ and fresh single-commit branches, never from feat/repair-x3d; always check the PR base before opening (the fork defaults to Web3DConsortium/x3d_mcp; accidental open-and-close PRs #33, #34, #35 are the precedent). A bounded huge_tree change, a 'not checkable at this size' verdict and a splat-slab-aware check are fork-only proposals until HagopJay types 'send'. Upstream asks (4.1 JSON schema, NavigationInfo.@type fix, @version enum, binary/URL splat payload, XSD >14 MB note) stay private, nothing goes to the Web3D Consortium or outside repos without his typed 'send'. x3d-blender-io is GPL-3.0 and public too: apply the same no-trailer care to any PR, and the commit attribution line mandated for this session applies only if I commit (I did not).

digests.summary: The slice is a finished, private 17 Oct 2026 programme: DSPy GEPA with the fork validator as the metric (d5598c4, X_ITE 16.5.0, 61 held-out prompts), then a deterministic repair ladder, an LLM-written ladder, and a GEPA-driven attacker. Headline numbers all verified on disk: flash first-try valid 34.4% (63/183) to 63.9% (117/183) with profile Full banned, 74.3% with Full allowed (26% of the gain was the exit); ladder 72.1 to 78.6% out-of-sample on 1,370 scenes and 83.7 to 86.9% (585/673) on a design/test split; attacker 332 attempts, 162 valid non-trivial, 82 gaps (valid by the fork, blank or erroring in X_ITE), nine named classes cover 71 (opaque GLSL 36 largest). The lesson that carries over is the ORDER OF EXITS (deterministic fix, better message, prompt rule, example) and that every metric has an exit an optimiser finds in its first mutation. I added hands-on Blender-side tests (bpy 5.2.3 LTS, x3d-blender-io 482741b, fork d5598c4, X_ITE 16.5.0 and 16.5.1): Blender import plus a Cycles render is a genuinely different oracle (it agrees with X_ITE on only 2 of 8 hidden-content reproducers), and a Blender round trip silently repairs or rewrites six of the eight blank classes; valid-but-wrong sci-vis fixtures (units, float32 offset, colour, splat SH) pass the fork or are silent on it, and I found 3 importer defects that any Blender-side metric would otherwise inherit. Missing/empty on disk: specs/*.md (empty dir), HANDOFF.md (absent in dspy folder); the three persistent specs live only as Claude Docs. Proposal below: a three-way (V, X, B) plus data-fidelity (D) metric ladder, four DSPy programs and six attacker families, roughly $25 total, Gemini/NVIDIA only, nothing run on paid APIs by me.

offers_to_blender: A tested optimisation harness (GEPA/DSPy 3.4.1, validator-as-metric, $0.008 per flash rollout) whose metric can be swapped for 'Blender import + Cycles render + data-fidelity check': gives bpy-script agents a measurable target, which the KB (section 6) says does not exist for Blender agents.

The exit-ordering method: for each recurring Blender-lane failure class use (1) a deterministic fixer, (2) a better tool message, (3) a prompt rule, (4) a retrieved example. Rungs are synthesised per generator family for about $0.10 and 3 minutes.

An attacker harness that produces valid-but-wrong cases on demand; I measured that Blender is a different oracle (agrees with X_ITE on 2 of 8 blank classes) so conjunctive checking closes loopholes neither side closes alone.

Concrete sci-vis valid-but-wrong fixtures (units, float32 offset, colour double-conversion, splat SH0-as-RGB, NaN position) with measured Blender-side values, ready as unit tests for importer/exporter PRs.

Judge infrastructure notes: picture judge on a 2x2 contact sheet costs about $0.0018 per call (165 calls = $0.29), kappa 0.82 between two judges, caveat that judges miss real defects; blank/dim thresholds and the dark-by-design trap (agent-loop-lessons).
offers_to_x3d: Blender-side evidence for validator hardening: fork d5598c4 is silent on head <unit conversionFactor> (0 occurrences in semantic.py and validate.py), on float32 magnitude loss, on splat SH0-as-RGB and quaternion component order, and its XSD layer raises (crash) on a NaN position in GaussianSplats; candidate lints drafted by measurement, not built.

digests.summary: The project already has a layered "exactness ladder" (proven > computed > judged) with measured pieces at every layer, but nothing sci-vis specific. Proven: fork validator and XSD. Computed: X_ITE non-blank check, object-ID masks, event-graph oracle, SSIM/PSNR/Delta-E between Cycles and X_ITE, camera-path recovery. Judged: Gemini, GPT and NVIDIA vision judges on contact sheets. Key measured facts: 203 of 1,058 valid library scenes draw nothing (fork d5598c4, X_ITE 16.5.0); M0 gave 304 of 310 view-0-blank valid scenes a named cause (98.1%), producing candidate "valid but invisible" rungs (Geo at Earth scale 24, HAnim joints containerField 12, all URLs unresolved 100, fragment root 3, colour equals background 22, out of view 94). Judges are noisy: the second-shown image wins about 60%, about a third of verdicts flip when order is swapped, only 1 of 3 judges passed a real-photo control, and identical pairs were given a winner 3 of 3 times. The "best model misses up to a quarter of real defects" number comes from judge-bench-v2 and is a TEXT judge of XSD validity on 20 scenes (10 valid), not a picture judge, so it must not be quoted for renders. Look parity: Blender 5.2.2 Cycles vs X_ITE 16.4.3 gave SSIM 0.9053, Delta-E2000 mean 4.50, PSNR 21.36 dB for a PBR still life (I re-ran it this session: Confirmed), splats 0.9767 / 29.28 dB / dE 1.43. Nobody has built a sci-vis loop (colour map equals data, legend present, splats visible), no Blender-import-direction parity is measured, and the picture-judge spec (Claude Doc f484ec0f, spec only, nothing run) has no sci-vis defect classes. The proposal below plugs sci-vis into that spec: computed data-colour and legend oracles first, panel judge last, each finding promoted to a validator rung or library tag.

digests.summary: The X3D side already has a working, measured agent architecture: a writer model, x3d_mcp tools or a bare XML answer, the fork validator (XSD plus semantic layer, reports with line and hint), a no-model autofix and repair_x3d, a report-back loop of at most 3 attempts, an X_ITE render check (watcher plus nonblank test) and a hash-chained ledger in the scene's own head/meta (x3dprov). The loop is implemented three times (playground/loop.py in the x3d_mcp fork, the Splat Park tools/agent_loop.py with validate/render/submit tools, and the Firehose live runs). The evidence is strongest for "valid is not visible is not right": three oracles are needed. Nothing in the Blender lane has this: the Blender MCP lane is an execute_code bridge with no artifact check, and x3d-blender-io's built-in export "validation" (source/validate.py) only checks the root tag, the version string and the presence of Scene. I ran a Blender-lane probe on bpy 5.2.3 (importer 482741b, fork 8dd0d3e): an agent-style bpy script exported to X3D 4.0 passed the validator with 0 errors and 0 warnings while silently losing three things (procedural texture, emission strength 5.0, sun energy 3.0). The ledger survived Blender import and re-export (7 of 7 head metas), and an unrecorded round trip reads "stale" until a transform step is added. So a Blender-lane agent fits the same tether if three things are added: a Blender-side loss audit that runs on the source .blend BEFORE export, a mandatory recorded transform step for every Blender hop, and ledger/Hall hash alignment. The Hall (3,058 panes: 957 lit, 1,835 dark, 260 split, 4 unread, 2 undecidable) is a ready memory and curriculum: every pane has a sha256 id, a verdict from two validators, the validators' top findings, 1,610 carry the prompt that made them, and 3 real before/after repair pairs exist for the lectern rite. In flight (do not duplicate): Blenderization, Accountability Playground (live since 16 Oct), Compact encodings, Scene Lab / x3d-coopilot (loop experiment built but NOT run, draft note waits for "send"), Firehose 4 (wave 2 of 3), Splat Park rev 6, and upstream-ready-v2 (17 patches, nothing sent). Not started: the Blender-MCP vs x3d_mcp A/B (KB test 6), any Blender-lane tool wrappers (bl_export_x3d, bl_loss_audit), provenance_stamp/verify tools in the fork, Hall write-back from the loop.

bridge_ideas.idea: UNIFIED AGENT LOOP, one tether with two writer lanes. Roles: ORCHESTRATOR (client, e.g. playground run_loop or Claude Code) is the only caller; no tool calls another. (1) WRITER, lane X: x3d_mcp granular/workflow tools or raw XML. WRITER, lane B: Blender MCP `execute_blender_code` run against a COPY of the .blend, script saved and hashed (script_sha256 -> ledger 'generate' step). (2) EXPORT (lane B only): `bl_export_x3d(version=4.0|4.1, ledger=scene['x3d_head_meta'])` wraps bpy.ops.export_scene.x3d from x3d-blender-io. The X3D, not the .blend, is the accountable artifact; its id is the Hall pane id. (3) LOSS AUDIT `bl_loss_audit(blend)` runs on the SOURCE before export (after a round trip the loss is invisible: audit_after_roundtrip was empty) and emits 'judge' ledger step. (4) ORACLE 1 `x3d_validate(xml)` = fork validator (XSD+semantic, line+hint). Proposed LangGraph spec. STATE (TypedDict): prompt_id, brief, writer_model, x3d_xml, validator_pin (d5598c4/eb4b4b4), report, repair_round, rungs_applied, render{patch,rig,lit_px,brightness_map}, judge{verdicts,order,tie,consensus}, ontology{findings}, blender{roundtrip_ok,diff}, cost_usd, cap_usd, lap_id, failure_class, human_gate. NODES: retrieve (BigQuery spine exemplars, search/Maps grounding facts) > writer (DSPy module, per-family rule pack) > mcp_tools (x3d_mcp validate/convert/inspect, in-process) > validate > repair_ladder (autofix then model repair, cap 2-3 rounds, call budget per family) > render (X_ITE 16.5.1 fly.mjs rig + M0 X3 blank cause + ID-mask) > ontology_check (use-type, Geo-vs-local viewpoint) > picture_judge (3 judges both orders, tie, consensus, control image) > blender_roundtrip (x3d-blender-io export/import/diff, glb check) > ledger (spend, funnel V>R>I, ledger.jsonl + BigQuery) > corpus_update (accept scene into library/exemplars; mine failure classes) > [lap-level] dspy_optimiser (GEPA/MIPRO on fresh held-out) and redteam (attacker lens claims/leaks/reader/agents). EDGES: validate-fail > repair_ladder > validate (loop until cap); validate-pass > render; render-blank > repair_ladder with cause text; render-ok > ontology_check > picture_judge > blender_roundtrip > ledger > corpus_update; judge/blender disagreement > human_gate (interrupt). TERMINATION: accepted (valid+draws+judge consensus), repair cap, cost cap, or lap stop rule (two laps under +3 points or loopholes opening faster than closing). CHECKPOINTS: per-node via checkpointer keyed thread_id=prompt_id, lap summary to BigQuery, interrupt before corpus_update and before anything bound for public fork.

catalog.thesis: PolyXandria is the place where the pieces that already turn separately meet in one loop: the x3d_mcp fork (exact validator plus Playground), the x3d-blender-io fork (the only modern Blender X3D path and the only splat exporter), the ontology (legal-parent and HAnim lookups), compact encodings, the DSPy/red-team programme, the agent loops, the AI-vision judges and the Library's 3,058-scene spine. The Blender sci-vis expert adds what none of them has: a second renderer and exact oracles (Cycles, BVH contact, ID masks), a source of known-answer sci-vis fixtures the Library cannot supply (0 clean valid PointSet, ColorRGBA, MetadataFloat or volume scenes; 5 clean splat scenes, SH0 only), and a guard for the Blender-agent lane. In return Blender gets the validator as a pre-import and post-export gate, the spine as a 585-scene on-disk importer regression set, mutants as fuzz input, X_ITE-exact look and animation oracles, and provenance that survives its round trip. Splats are the first and best-proven wire (PLY to X3D 4.1 to Blender to PLY is float32-exact on bpy 5.2.3, with measured walls and ordering traps). The main missing pieces are instrumentation and wiring, not new science: per-hop metrics, a durable fixture suite, a Blender-side loss audit, and a LangGraph graph that calls the existing scripts as nodes. Almost all of it runs at $0 in this container (bpy 5.2.3, fork validator, headless Chromium X_ITE 16.5.1), and most fork changes are handoffs to the in-flight Blenderization and Playground threads, not new builds.

L2 Importer/exporter defect loop: Library corpus (585 on-disk, Tier A 111) + spine mutants -> round-trip ledger -> value-level defects (colour, defaults, crashes) -> Blenderization fixes -> better Hall renders and calibration -> sharper fixtures.

L3 Tether/guard loop: Blender agent script -> loss audit -> export -> pinned validator -> X_ITE + Blender render -> ledger step -> failures become loss-audit rules, lints and ladder rungs, which gate the next agent script.

L4 Oracle ladder loop: computed oracles (ID mask, blank cause, splat oracle, BVH) take over from judges, so judge noise (second image wins 60%, ~1/3 order flips) stops being the bottleneck; the residual goes to the panel.

L6 Provenance/Library loop: every hop (generate, export, validate, render, judge) is an x3dprov step; accepted scenes and figures are written back to the Library with lineage and licence passport, growing exemplars, mutants and curricula.

problems: Alpha criterion (<= 1e-6) is not backed on disk. splat-trailer/work/rt_2000.json records opacity_logit max abs diff 2.7e-4 to 6.8e-4 (e.g. SH3 6.85e-4) for both mesh and pointcloud. That is a logit-space error. Alpha-space error is not recorded. Bounded by sigmoid' <= 0.25 it could be up to about 1.7e-4, so 1e-6 is unverified and probably too tight. Use a logit tolerance of about 1e-3 (or an alpha tolerance of about 2e-4) until alpha is measured.

Logit clamp: in the 323,295-splat Sphinx run (real_sphinx_mesh.json) 33,612 splats have a logit above 13.8155 (range -3.89 to 18.18). So the Sphinx fixture will not round-trip alpha exactly. It needs its own expected-loss row, not just a footnote.

Splat count mismatch: rt_2000.json used N=2000 (ply bytes 136414, 208630, 329004, 497529 for SH0 to SH3). The 3,125-splat seed-1741 fixture is a different set (fx3/S1_sh*, fx4/D8B.stats.json splats_in 3125). The M1/M2 'max abs diff 0' claim was read only from the N=2000 run. The fx3 3,125 PLYs were not re-run through the round trip here.

PSNR range: I recomputed it with bpy from fx3/refc_sh{0..3}_{A_front,B_oblique,C_close}.png against fx3/x1651_sh*/*.png. The minimum is 46.17 (SH3 B_oblique), as claimed. bridge.title: Validator: huge_tree in validate_xml plus honest 'not checkable at this size' verdict
bridge.what: validate.py:183 parses without huge_tree while semantic.py already uses it, so any GaussianSplats start tag over about 10 MB is falsely reported INVALID (all Blender splat exports above ~64k SH0 or ~14k SH3 text splats). One-line fix or an explicit not-checkable verdict, plus a regression fixture.
inputs: x3d_mcp src/validation/validate.py line 183 and semantic.py line 1020
bridge.deliverable: Trailer-free patch (parser with huge_tree=True, resolve_entities=False, no_network=True) and a 16,000-SH3 fixture for the Playground scoreboard; proposal only until HagopJay types send.
bridge.test_and_pass_criteria: Unpatched validate_xml fails 'Buffer size limit exceeded' at 41000 SH1 (10.56 MB) and 16000 SH3 (10.72 MB) and passes 36000 SH1 / 14000 SH3; patched copy accepts both. Also note one attribute above ~13.5 MB still hits the XSD engine Internal error even with huge_tree.
bridge.pins: fork 688174f, d5598c4, main 8dd0d3e and upstream 74da0ec all fail identically (lxml 6.1.3, libxml2 2.14.6)
bridge.owner_thread_or_repo: Accountability Playground thread (x3d_mcp fork, PUBLIC: no AI trailers) - handoff, not a build
bridge.visual_fidelity_angle: Removes a false INVALID on exactly the high-fidelity splat files (Marble, Pantheon 500k, Sphinx) that need the most checking.

problems: Commit pins do not match what is on disk: the checkouts I ran are 8dd0d3e (x3d-ml/fork and x3d-ml/x3d_mcp), d5598c4 (dspy-redteam/fork_d5598c4) and 74da0ec (x3d-ml/upstream_x3d_mcp). I found no checkout at 688174f or eb4b4b4, so those two pins are unverified. The bridge's 'main 8dd0d3e' conflicts with the workflow's 'main eb4b4b4'.

Upstream 74da0ec differs structurally: its fromstring is at validate.py:57, not 183, and src/validation/semantic.py there has no huge_tree. The 'line 183' and 'semantic.py already uses huge_tree' claims hold only for the fork-lineage 8dd0d3e/d5598c4. Upstream fails identically, with the same error and column.

The limit is per attribute or text node (error at line 5, column 10003666, inside the 'orientations' attribute, 1.84 MB), not per file or start tag. The 41000 SH1 and 16000 SH3 files fail because one attribute crosses the 10,000,000-byte limit, not because the file passes 10 MB. The wording 'start tag over about 10 MB' is slightly off.

The XSD Internal error is not a verdict. validate_xml raises XMLSchemaValidateError uncaught, so a caller sees an exception, not valid:false. I measured: 12 MB single attribute passes, 13.5 MB or more raises. The threshold is therefore between 12 and 13.5 MB, and '~13.5' is an upper bound. The patch should catch it and return an explicit 'not checkable at this size' verdict.

Patched timing: 41000 SH1 took 1.0 s patched. The unpatched 36000 SH1 run took 3.0 s; I did not time patched 36000 separately. The fixture that matters for the scoreboard is 16000 SH3, 10,719,036 bytes.
verdicts.notes: Reproduced with lxml 6.1.3 / libxml2 2.14.6 (x3d-mcp-fork/venv). Unpatched validate_xml at 8dd0d3e and d5598c4 gives: n36000_sh1 (9,273,339 B) valid; n41000_sh1 (10,561,301 B) invalid with 'Buffer size limit exceeded'; n14000_sh3 (9,378,980 B) valid; n16000_sh3 (10,719,036 B) invalid with the same error. Upstream 74da0ec gives the same four results. Patching only the Step 1 parse to XMLParser(huge_tree=True, resolve_entities=False, no_network=True) makes all four valid (schema 4.1). That parser matches semantic.py:1020 exactly, and the comment at semantic.py:1017 says huge_tree lifts the 10 MB limit. All cited inputs exist: scratchpad/hall-build/huge/{n36000_sh1,n41000_sh1,n14000_sh3,n16000_sh3}.x3d and scratchpad/blender-io/tools/gen_splat_x3d.py (I only checked it exists, not its contents). The ~13.5 MB XSD Internal error is reproduced, but as an uncaught exception (see problems). The central claim is Confirmed on disk. Only the pin list is imprecise, because 688174f and eb4b4b4 have no local checkout. I ran only the XSD validate_xml path, with no X_ITE rendering, so no X_ITE patch applies. The scratch test script is at scratchpad/b02/t.py. The grade stays Confirmed.

problems: Already tracked, not new: /mnt/project-files/ops/tracker/BOARD.md BUG-2 (P2, open, Validator, opened 2026-10-11) is the same defect ('Use huge_tree in validate.py too, or report not checkable at this size'). It says a ready patch (+63/-5) and an xmlschema fallback from the Splat Park thread already exist, and the Pantheon 500k validates in 9.1 s. The bridge does not mention BUG-2 or Splat Park, and should be reframed as a handoff or evidence-add to BUG-2.

Silo memory already records the same facts: giza-x3d-showpiece.md:16 (fork validate_xml needs huge_tree), x3d-mcp-fork-branches.md:15 (huge_tree at validate.py:183), x3d-bench-next-levels.md:16 (XSD fails at ~13.5 MB per attribute, ~360k splats). The '~13.5 MB attribute still hits XSD Internal error' note is therefore not new.

Line-number and pin inconsistencies. The bridge cites semantic.py:1020 and 'main 8dd0d3e'. In the scratchpad clone (HEAD 8dd0d3e, 'Merge pull request #11 from hagsmac/fix/physics-findings'), semantic.py:1020 is _PARSER = XMLParser(huge_tree=True, resolve_entities=False, no_network=True) and validate.py:183 is etree.fromstring without huge_tree. BOARD.md cites semantic.py:910 on fork main eb4b4b4. The standing pin is eb4b4b4, and 8dd0d3e is not in the memory notes. Quote one pin per number, and say that 8dd0d3e comes from a clone whose HEAD is a merge of a PR from the hagsmac account (provenance unclear).

The threshold numbers (about 10 MB; 41000 SH1 = 10.56 MB; 16000 SH3 = 10.72 MB) are the bridge's own measurements. I did not re-run them. BOARD.md has different earlier numbers (80k pass / 90k fail), so cite only the new fixture sizes as new evidence.

Rule check is clean. $0, no GCP, no OpenAI, no outside-repo write, no deletion. The x3d_mcp fork is public, so the 'trailer-free, proposal until send' wording is right and the deliverable must carry no AI trailers. The 'S' effort is realistic for the one-line parser change, plus a regression test and fixture.

Owner is wrong or incomplete. BUG-2 belongs to the Validator workstream, and the patch to reuse comes from the Splat Park thread. The bridge names the Accountability Playground thread, which already merged PR #6 (fork main eb4b4b4), so follow-up work restarts from main.
verdicts.notes: Lens verdict: no rule violation, but this is a duplicate. Treat it as a handoff to the existing BUG-2 / Splat Park patch, not a new bridge. What the bridge adds is a regression fixture (16000 SH3, about 10.7 MB, right at the 10 MB wall; 41000 SH1) and the Blender-export framing (above ~64k SH0 or ~14k SH3 text splats). Confirmed on disk: validate.py:183 has no huge_tree in the scratchpad clone at 8dd0d3e, and semantic.py:1020 has huge_tree=True with resolve_entities=False and no_network=True. Confirmed in BOARD.md: BUG-2 is open and a ready patch exists. Not re-run by me: the byte-level thresholds and the 'all four pins fail identically' claim (fork 688174f, d5598c4, main 8dd0d3e, upstream 74da0ec). The grade drops from Confirmed to Likely for those unverified numbers. Suggested next step: ask the Splat Park thread for the +63/-5 patch, add the two new fixtures as test cases, and propose only after HagopJay types 'send'. bridge.title: Exporter option: max bytes per GaussianSplats node (depth slabs / spatial cells) with bbox fields

bridge.pins: x3d-blender-io 482741b; fork 688174f/d5598c4, upstream 74da0ec; X_ITE 16.5.0 and 16.5.1 (hang reproduced on both and 16.6.0)
bridge.visual_fidelity_angle: Node order decides quality: file-order nodes 19.06 dB vs depth slabs 26.35 dB (Anamnesis, X_ITE 16.5.0), so slab geometry is a fidelity feature, not just a size fix.

problems: Could not find '154.5 B per SH0 splat' anywhere on disk (HALL.md, CAPTURE-LOG.md, scratch JSON/logs). Nearest on-disk figure is d1000: 152,733,317 bytes / 1,000,000 splats = 152.7 B (CAPTURE-LOG.md line 57), and d640 97,378,148/640,000 = 152.2 B. The SH level of those shots is not stated on the lines I read.
Could not find the '~65k over the wall' threshold in the memory files or the HALL log. The 10 MB lxml huge_tree limit is a plausible source but I did not read the line.

The 19.06 vs 26.35 dB figures are real (HALL.md line 190; CAPTURE-LOG.md lines 55 and 58) but they are PSNR against the trainer's own frame of the bar-16 pose, not against a single-node X_ITE baseline. They compare file-order k640 against depth-slab d640 at 640k splats, 13 nodes of 50,000 (not 100k or 323k). 26.32 dB was measured on X_ITE 16.5.1 on SwiftShader at 960x540 and 19.17 for file order at that size. So 'X_ITE 16.5.0' in the bridge text is only partly accurate.

make_presets_depth.py slabs are view-pose dependent (--depth-order along the shot's DIR). They fit a fixed camera and do not give free walking. Only make_presets_walk.py --spatial (cells plus --cull-off) is view-independent, so the exporter's default has to be cell mode, as the bridge says. The fidelity claim for depth slabs does not carry over to cell mode untested.
The pass criterion 'PSNR within 1 dB of single-node baseline' has no baseline on disk. A single node at 640k is not possible, so the baseline must be a small splat count that fits in one node.

The 'hang reproduced on 16.5.0, 16.5.1 and 16.6.0' claim was not checked. I only saw the docstring in make_presets_walk.py line 3 ('loadURL never resolves when a cell is out of view'). I did not look for a 16.6.0 record.

The inputs list names 'splat-trailer/work/mp/' without saying it holds only src/ (copies of the two make_presets scripts) and repos/x3d-blender-io. A prototype patch against 482741b is therefore feasible but does not exist yet.

The reference '1M in 20 nodes valid on 688174f/74da0ec' is Confirmed (CAPTURE-LOG.md line 57). But the validators were not run on d5598c4 in that log, so the d5598c4 criterion is new work. The criterion 'without huge_tree' is not tested by that row either.
verdicts.notes: Central claim verified: the exporter has no slabbing or bbox at 482741b. In scratch repo /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/265b8e8b-423c-5c89-85e0-1bdddc0f5797/scratchpad/splat-trailer/work/mp/repos/x3d-blender-io (HEAD 482741b, 'Merge pull request #24'), source/emit_x3d40.py lines 599-621 (_splats_xml) emit one <GaussianSplats> node with positions/scales/orientations/opacities/SH. There is no bboxCenter or bboxSize, and a grep for bbox, chunk and max_per across source/ finds nothing. The port sources exist: /mnt/project-files/polyxandria/library/trailer/src/make_presets_depth.py (bboxCenter/bboxSize lines 113-118, --chunk default 50000) and make_presets_walk.py (recursive median cells, --cull-off, lines 3-5, 140-142, 162). big_export.py is in scratchpad/splat-trailer/work/. Reference numbers confirmed: d1000 has 1,000,000 splats in 20 nodes at 152.7 MB, valid with 0 errors and 0 warnings on fork 688174f and upstream 74da0ec, X_ITE 16.5.0 and 16.5.1 pixel-identical, PSNR 27.82 dB (CAPTURE-LOG.md line 57). d640 is 13 nodes, 26.35 dB. The file-order k640 scored 19.06 dB (HALL.md lines 189-190). The grade is lowered from Confirmed to Likely because of the unverifiable 154.5 B and ~65k figures, the pose-dependence of depth slabs, the missing single-node baseline, and the unverified 16.6.0 hang. The 100k and 323k fixtures and d5598c4 validation do not exist yet."

problems: Grade 'Confirmed' is too strong for the whole bridge. I could not find the '1M splats in 20 nodes valid on 688174f/74da0ec' reference or the '154.5 B per SH0 splat' number in silo memory or the x3d-blender-io clone. Both need a pointer to a log or file.

The 19.06 dB vs 26.35 dB figure is documented in library-hall-build.md line 15 as 19.1 vs 26.3 dB. It is X_ITE 16.5.0 on Anamnesis views only. Quote it with that patch and do not reuse it as the 16.5.1 pass criterion without re-measuring.

make_presets_depth.py slabs by view depth, so the slabs depend on one camera (bboxCenter sits on the view ray). An exporter has no camera. Depth-slab mode needs an explicit camera or viewpoint input, or a fallback to the spatial-cell mode from make_presets_walk.py (--spatial N --cull-off). Only the spatial-cell mode gives free-walk ordering. The note should say this, and the 'within 1 dB of baseline' PSNR criterion only makes sense per fixed pose.

Fork validator limits: silo notes say fork c9c9788 needs huge_tree above 10 MB, and splat nodes over ~77k are reported as an XML parse error (10 MB start tag). The pass criterion 'no huge_tree' is plausible for <=25k/<=50k per node (~5-8 MB per tag). Re-test it on d5598c4 and 74da0ec, not on c9c9788. I did not run it.

The dependency B01-RT-SPLAT-LADDER may be the real source of the 100k and 323k fixtures. The 323,295-splat / 42.2 MB 2-node file is from sphinx-gpu-run.md (a GCP run). Reuse that existing PLY or X3D and do not regenerate on GCP.
Effort M is realistic for the code and tests. The X_ITE oracle runs on 8 and 64 cells with 16.5.0 and 16.5.1 are SwiftShader renders and are slow (about 20 s load per 42 MB file). Budget for that.

bridge.title: Licence passport on Blender exports and classifier fixes
bridge.what: Exporter writes creator, licence, generator version and source sha256 in head meta by default so Blender-made files enter the spine as 'converted' lineage and can be clean; teach collect.py GPL/LGPL/Unlicense and treat CC BY-ND as restricted for derivatives.
bridge.deliverable: Classifier test strings plus exporter default proposal.
bridge.test_and_pass_criteria: Classifier table: 'GNU GPL v3', 'GNU LGPL v3', 'Unlicense', 'NONE' no longer read unknown; 'CC BY-ND 4.0' not permissive; all 11 Blender-export spine scenes classify.
bridge.owner_thread_or_repo: Library / spine thread; exporter default is Blenderization handoff
bridge.visual_fidelity_angle: None direct; enables Blender-made reference scenes to enter shareable corpora.

problems: Scope correction: only 7 of the 11 blender_export scenes are fork exports (blender-x3d/milestone-1/*, licence_raw 'NONE', snapshot licence 'unknown'). The other 4 are blender-x3d/prior-work/x3d_gltf/demo/investor_poc/*.x3d, creator 'OpenAI Codex', snapshot licence 'none'. They are not output of the Blender exporter, and no classifier change moves them.

'All 11 classify' is already true in the sense of a status being assigned: 7 'unknown', 4 'none'. The real pass criterion is that the 7 'NONE' scenes read 'none' rather than 'unknown'. The 4 Codex scenes need a creator or licence in the source, not a classifier fix.

Becoming 'clean' needs more than a licence. In snapshot_v1.jsonl all 11 have clean=false, and 6 of the 11 have fork=invalid (swatch-book, cube, scene-fixture, hanim-fixture, part, blender_modern_poc), as read at the snapshot's validator pins. A licence passport alone will not make them clean.

Exporter gap is larger than stated. There is no sha256 or hashlib anywhere in x3d-blender-io/source/*.py. The creator meta is written only if the user fills meta_creator (export_x3d.py ~L339). Generator ('generator') and translator metas are already written (L368-370), so those are not new. The licence meta is skipped when the enum is NONE (L352), though the milestone-1 fixtures still carry license=NONE via the emit_x3d40 path (emit_x3d40.py L676).

'GNU GPL v3' is an exporter menu string (translations.py L118). Nothing in the classifier regexes matches GPL, LGPL or Unlicense, but the fork's own licence dropdown can produce them. This confirms the gap and it is a real exporter-to-spine mismatch.
verdicts.notes:
Central claims verified on disk.

Classifier: /mnt/project-files/spine/ingest/collect.py L25-26 holds LICENCE_PERMISSIVE and LICENCE_RESTRICT. L82-87 licence_status returns 'unknown' when neither matches. I ran the two regexes on the test strings:
- 'GNU GPL v3', 'GNU LGPL v3', 'Unlicense', 'The Unlicense' and 'NONE' match neither regex, so all read 'unknown'. Confirmed.
- 'CC BY-ND 4.0' matches PERMISSIVE via cc-by and does not match RESTRICT, so it currently reads explicit_permissive. Confirmed, and wrong for derivatives.
- 'CC BY-NC 4.0' already reads restricted, which is correct.
- 'Public Domain' is permissive.

The fork's licence dropdown (x3d-blender-io source/__init__.py L388 onward) offers these enum values: NONE, CUSTOM, CC_BY_4.0, CC_BY-SA_4.0, CC_BY-NC_4.0, CC0_1.0, CC_BY-ND_4.0, GPL_v3, GPL_v2, LGPL_v3, LGPL_v2.1, MIT, Apache, BSD_3/2/1, Mozilla_2.0, Pixar, Standard_Royalty-Free, Extended_Commercial, Public_Domain, Unlicense, NOSA_1.3. Display names are in translations.py L113-131.

Classifier gaps beyond the four named in the bridge. These strings also hit the permissive 'open source' / 'bsd' / 'mit' tokens or nothing at all, and the audit should cover all of them:
- GPL v2 and LGPL v2.1 read 'unknown'.
- Mozilla, Pixar and NOSA read 'unknown'.
- 'CC BY-SA' reads permissive. That is arguably fine, but share-alike should be flagged.
- 'Standard Royalty-Free' and 'Extended Commercial' read 'unknown', and the exporter writes 'All rights reserved' only in the copyright meta. 'CUSTOM' is similar.

Exporter proposal is feasible. It would be a small addition to the head block at export_x3d.py L335-370, plus the equivalent in emit_x3d40.py, with a default creator and a source sha256 meta.

Validator pins: the snapshot_v1.jsonl numbers come from the fork and upstream (up) validator columns, which the bridge pins to 688174f/74da0ec. I did not re-run any validator. The blender_export count is 11 of 3058 rows (grep -c and python). X_ITE patch is not relevant to this bridge.

The bridge's 'GPL/LGPL/Unlicense/NONE no longer unknown' criterion needs a decision on what NONE maps to. I recommend 'none' (no licence stated), which is the status the 4 Codex scenes already have. I made no repo or disk changes; scratch clone is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/265b8e8b-423c-5c89-85e0-1bdddc0f5797/scratchpad/b17/x3d-blender-io.

problems: Exporter-default half (head meta in x3d-blender-io __init__.py) is a Blenderization-thread handoff, and a public-fork change must carry no AI trailers; do not implement it here.

Pass criterion 'all 11 Blender-export scenes classify' is partly mis-framed: classify() only reads licence_raw; scenes with no meta (e.g. xite_whopper_inline_poc.x3d, licence 'none') stay 'none' until the exporter writes meta. Reword as 'none -> explicit after re-export'.

Also fix the 'mit\b' substring false positive (matches 'Permit', 'submit') and note 'usable_for_training' in build_rows.py:37 keys on explicit_permissive, so CC BY-ND flip changes training eligibility; confirm the policy with HagopJay.
Adding 'copyleft' status for GPL/LGPL needs a rule on whether usable_for_training; unspecified in the bridge.
Spine ingest sits in /mnt/project-files (read-only for this workflow), so the collect.py edit must be a proposal diff to the Library/spine owner, not applied by readers.
verdicts.notes: No rule violation: $0, no GCP/OpenAI/outside write/deletion; no duplicate found (grep of silo memory for passport/GPL/collect.py classifier turned up nothing; only a bench-forensics mention of collect.py). Reproduced against /mnt/project-files/spine/ingest/collect.py lines 25-26 and 82-87 (LICENCE_PERMISSIVE / LICENCE_RESTRICT regexes, licence_status()). Ran those exact regexes: 'GNU GPL v3', 'GNU LGPL v3', 'Unlicense', 'NONE' match neither pattern, so they return 'unknown'. 'CC BY-ND 4.0' matches cc[- ]?by, so it returns explicit_permissive (real bug; the NC test only catches cc-by-nc). 'Permit use' also reads permissive via 'mit\b'. snapshot_v1.jsonl has 11 kind=blender_export rows (grep count 11; rows carry licence/clean/creator fields, e.g. the xite_whopper_inline_poc row has licence 'none', creator 'OpenAI Codex', clean false). I did not re-verify the validator pin (688174f/74da0ec); the classifier work does not depend on the validator. Effort S is realistic for the classifier (about 10 regex lines plus a test table); the exporter default is separate and belongs to the Blenderization thread. Recommend splitting B17 into B17a (classifier fixes plus tests, Library/spine thread) and B17b (exporter meta default, handoff). Grade stays Confirmed for the classifier half; the exporter line-388 claim I did not open.
